alignments.note: Proper name; the ASV fronts the subject.

The age formula ben + numeral + shanah: the construct `בֶּן` is what the ASV's *was ... old* renders, discontinuous around the numeral phrase under rule 25. Head on *old*, the word carrying the age relation, since *was* is the construction's copula (rule 20). No `הָיָה` stands in this verse to take the copula, unlike 27:8.
Numeral.
The units-to-tens waw takes the single written *and*, which stands between *twenty* and *five* (rule 42).
Numeral.
Counted noun of the first numeral phrase, rendered *years*.
Temporal `בְּ` + infinitive construct recast as a finite clause takes the *when* (rule 52).
Infinitive construct; the ingressive *began to reign* is its rendering, headed on the lexical verb *reign* (rule 24).
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun (rule 18).
Conjunction.
`שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה` is written in two morphemes and rendered by the single English word *sixteen*, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met; headed on `שֵׁשׁ`, which carries the lexeme.
Counted noun of the second numeral phrase.
Finite verb with its English subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.
Preposition.
Proper name.
Conjunction.
Construct noun; the ASV recasts the chain as an English possessive, so `שֵׁם` keeps only its own word.
The rectum, written as the English possessive *mother's*; the possessive marking is part of this word.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive *his* (rule 18); no article morpheme stands in the phrase, so nothing competes for it.
Predicate of the verbless clause; the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate (rule 20).
Construct noun with no article morpheme present, so the supplied *the* joins it (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).

review_notes: Age formula aligned with `בֶּן` carrying *was ... old*; 27:8 writes `הָיָה` and is divided differently there, as that verse's own evidence requires.
The one written *and* of the numeral phrase stands between *twenty* and *five*, so the units-to-tens waw takes it (rule 42); no second waw is present here.
